title: Lesson 14: Unit 1 Assessment, Part I: Reading and Answering Questions about Kitten's First Full Moon
objective: Students will listen to a story read aloud, identify and describe characters and setting, answer questions about key details, participate in role-play to understand major events and central message, and write responses about the story.

what_is_taught.skill: identify the main character of a story
describe the main character using story details
identify the setting of a story
describe the setting using story details
answer questions about key details from a story
write responses using pictures and words to show thinking about story elements
use sentence frames to support writing about story details
participate in role-play to act out major events of a story
discuss and explain the central message of a story
reflect on learning progress using a protocol
participate in group singing and movement to reinforce learning

student_actions.recognition_identification: Students identify characters and settings in the story and recognize story elements on charts and response sheets.
student_actions.oral_production: Students orally describe characters and settings, answer questions, share out with the group, participate in role-play, and sing the song with motions.
student_actions.written_production: Students write responses to prompts about the main character and setting using pictures and words, and write sentences explaining their word choice with support from sentence frames.
student_actions.procedural_application: Students apply the Role-Play protocol to act out story events and use sentence frames to write about story details.
student_actions.investigation_handson: Students engage in movement routines and use puppets to act out story events.
student_actions.representation_modeling: Students use charts and boards to represent story elements and use sentence frames to model writing.
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: Students explain why they chose certain words to describe the character using evidence from pictures and discuss the central message of the story.
student_actions.comprehension_response: Students respond to questions about key details, describe story elements, and reflect on their learning progress using the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol and group discussion about learning targets and next steps in learning progressions, orally and in writing as appropriate for the task and support provided.

evidence.quote: Invite students to the whole group area.
Direct students' attention to the Sun Movement chart and invite a student volunteer to lead the class through one round of the Sun Movement routine.
Direct students' attention to the posted learning targets and read the first one aloud: 'I can ask and answer questions about key details from Kitten's First Full Moon.'
'Who is the main character of this story? How would you describe the character?' (Kitten; curious, adventurous, brave, a cat with white fur)
Invite students to complete Part I of the Unit 1 Assessment response sheet. Remind them that they should use pictures and words to show their thinking.
Invite students to circle the word they think best describes how Kitten is acting in the pictures displayed on the Kitten's First Full Moon chart.
Tell students to write one or two sentences to describe how Kitten is acting and to explain what, from the pictures, helped them.
Move students into pre-determined pairs and tell them they are going to use the Role-Play protocol to act out a few of the major events of Kitten's First Full Moon.
Distribute Kitten's First Full Moon puppets and guide students through the protocol for the following sections of text: -Pages 1-2 -Pages 7-8 -Pages 11-12 -Pages 19-22 -Pages 27-28

'After rereading and acting out these parts of the text, what do you notice about the moon in this story?' (Kitten thinks it is a bowl of milk and she tries to get it, but she can't. The moon stays in the same place the whole time.)
'Why couldn't Kitten get the first bowl of milk she saw?' (The bowl of milk was actually the moon and the moon is in the sky, so Kitten couldn't get it.)
'How did you rate yourself on the learning targets? Why?' (Responses will vary.)
'What do you think you need to do next time to do even better?' (Responses will vary.)
Tell students they will end the lesson singing the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' Version 2 song to celebrate their hard work during this lesson and all the previous lessons.

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: The teacher models reading the story aloud fluently and with minimal interruption, reads learning targets aloud, guides students through movement routines and role-play protocols, provides sentence frames for writing, and leads reflection protocols.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: Who is the main character of this story? How would you describe the character?
What is the setting of this story? Where and when does the story take place?
After rereading and acting out these parts of the text, what do you notice about the moon in this story?
Why couldn't Kitten get the first bowl of milk she saw?
How did you rate yourself on the learning targets? Why?
What do you think you need to do next time to do even better?
